key_sources: What Works Clearinghouse, U.S. Department of Education. (2014). Repeated Reading: WWC Intervention Report, Students with Learning Disabilities. https://ies.ed.gov/ncee/wwc/InterventionReport/576

article_title: Reading Recovery®
citation: What Works Clearinghouse, Institute of Education Sciences, U.S. Department of Education. (2023, June). Reading Recovery® Intervention Report | English Language Arts Topic Area. https://whatworks.ed.gov
title: Reading Recovery training cascade: university-affiliated teacher training sites, teacher leaders, and certified teachers
description: Reading Recovery® sustains implementation through a three-level training infrastructure. Teacher training sites in public schools, affiliated with partnering universities, house teacher leaders who train teachers. Teacher leaders complete a yearlong training of graduate coursework and supervised practicums, and are expected to "provide initial training for up to 15 teacher candidates and provide ongoing support for 40 to 60 Reading Recovery® teachers or teachers in training annually." Teachers complete a yearlong graduate-credit training and must maintain registration by teaching at least eight students per year and participating in ongoing professional development.
requirements: Teacher leaders hold a master's degree and teaching credentials and complete a yearlong certification training
Teachers must be certified, experienced early elementary teachers and complete a year of training with graduate credit
Teachers must maintain registration by teaching at least eight students per year and attending ongoing professional development, typically no less than six sessions per school year
constraints: Neither contributing study provided details about the Reading Recovery® teacher training sites or the training of teacher leaders
Registration lapses after 1 year if teachers do not maintain the requirements
target_learners: Grade 1 students with low literacy achievement in districts implementing Reading Recovery®
target_learning_goals: Early literacy intervention delivered with training fidelity
examples: Based on survey results from one study, teacher leaders met 87% of the implementation standards, including attending 73% of training sessions and 98% of professional development sessions
key_sources: What Works Clearinghouse, Institute of Education Sciences, U.S. Department of Education. (2023, June). Reading Recovery® Intervention Report | English Language Arts Topic Area. https://ies.ed.gov/ncee/wwc/InterventionReport/730

article_title: eMINTS Comprehensive Program
citation: What Works Clearinghouse, Institute of Education Sciences, U.S. Department of Education. (2020). eMINTS Comprehensive Program Intervention Report │ Teacher Excellence Topic Area. NCEE WWC 2020-011. https://whatworks.ed.gov
title: Four-component design of eMINTS: sequenced professional development, coaching, technology integration, and online resources
description: The report enumerates four key components of eMINTS. Sequenced professional development delivers "approximately 140 hours of professional development focused on integrating technology into the classroom and developing lessons that use inquiry-based learning" over 2 or more years. Coaching provides one-on-one classroom sessions by instructional specialists plus group coaching to build school learning communities. Technology integration supports inquiry-based instruction, differentiated learning, and assessment. Online resources supply an eMINTS portal with assessments, lesson plans, example classroom websites, and online courses.
requirements: Trained instructional specialists to deliver professional development and coaching
Individual student access to Internet-connected computers or tablets for technology integration
constraints: A shorter version, eMINTS4All, includes fewer professional development sessions and coaching visits
target_learning_goals: Building a community of learning in schools
examples: At the end of the first year, teachers develop a classroom website with the help of the instructional specialist as a resource for students and their families
key_sources: What Works Clearinghouse, Institute of Education Sciences, U.S. Department of Education. (2020). eMINTS Comprehensive Program Intervention Report │ Teacher Excellence Topic Area. NCEE WWC 2020-011. https://ies.ed.gov/ncee/wwc/InterventionReport/705

article_title: Building Blocksâ"¢
citation: What Works Clearinghouse, Institute of Education Sciences, U.S. Department of Education. (2023, December). Building Blocks. https://whatworks.ed.gov
title: Building Blocks multi-context implementation pattern: whole-group, small-group, centers, computer activities, and family letters
description: The curriculum distributes mathematics learning across several classroom contexts: whole-group instruction during circle time (approximately 5–15 minutes, four or five times per week), small-group instruction with 3 to 6 children (approximately 10–15 minutes, two or three times per week), hands-on center activities, and computer activities that "automatically adjust when children progress well or need additional help." Weekly family/caregiver letters describe the mathematics and home activities. This pattern lets teachers adapt activities to children's developmental levels while other children work independently.
requirements: Teachers used the Teacher’s Edition to locate relevant activities.
Teachers received 4–8 full days of initial training, monthly 2-hour refresher classes, and on-site coaching 1–2 times a month.
constraints: Center activities were mostly free-choice, so frequency and duration varied; the content and duration of professional development varied across the studies.
target_learning_goals: early mathematics knowledge aligned to learning trajectories
examples: In the three contributing studies, children in the comparison group were taught by teachers who did not participate in Building Blocks training and did not implement the Building Blocks sessions.
key_sources: What Works Clearinghouse, Institute of Education Sciences, U.S. Department of Education. (2023, December). Building Blocks. https://ies.ed.gov/ncee/wwc/InterventionReport/733

article_title: Really Great Reading's Foundational Literacy Programs
citation: Really Great Reading. (2023). Really Great Reading. https://www.reallygreatreading.com
title: Deliver foundational literacy instruction with existing classroom staff and no additional personnel
description: RGR is designed so that "Classroom teachers, paraprofessionals, or tutors can deliver instruction" and "No additional staff is required." This staffing model keeps implementation feasible within existing school resources, complementing the program's emphasis on efficient instruction and minimized teacher preparation time through digital lesson delivery tools.
requirements: Delivery by classroom teachers, paraprofessionals, or tutors already present in the school
target_learners: Early elementary students receiving Tier 1, Tier 2, or Tier 3 support
target_learning_goals: Foundational reading skills including phonics and fluency
examples: The studied implementation assigned instruction to regular classroom teachers across 13 schools
key_sources: Really Great Reading. (2023). Really Great Reading. https://www.reallygreatreading.com

article_title: PAX Good Behavior Game — Reading
citation: Evidence for Learning. (2023). PAX Good Behavior Game (Evidence Rating). https://evidenceforlearning.org
title: Team-based group contingency for behavior management
description: The PAX Good Behavior Game organizes classroom behavior management around a group contingency: students are divided into two or more teams, and when a member violates class rules "discussed and agreed upon by the students themselves", the team receives a check mark. The team with the fewest checkmarks, or all teams meeting a set criterion, receives a small privilege such as lining up first for recess. This structure is "intended to create a situation in which students encourage and assist their peers to behave appropriately".
requirements: class rules discussed and agreed upon by the students themselves
teacher monitoring of student behavior
small privileges as reinforcers
examples: Teams receive checkmarks on a whiteboard for rule violations; the winning team or all qualifying teams receive a small privilege such as lining up first for recess.
key_sources: Evidence for Learning. (2023). PAX Good Behavior Game (Evidence Rating). https://evidenceforessa.org/program/pax-good-behavior-game-reading/

article_title: Corrective Reading — Elementary
citation: Corrective Reading. (2021). https://www.evidenceforessa.org/
title: Deliver Corrective Reading in small groups with sessions 4-5 days per week for optimal achievement gains
description: The article states the program "is most effective when taught in small groups" and that "Sessions should occur 4-5 days per week for optimal achievement gains". Delivery can occur inside or outside the regular classroom, and instructors may teach multiple groups across the school day.
requirements: Instructors may include general classroom teachers, special education teachers, intervention specialists, and paraprofessionals
constraints: The frequency recommendation reflects the article's stated conditions for optimal achievement gains, not a tested comparison in the summary
target_learners: Upper-elementary struggling readers in small intervention groups
examples: Lesson delivery can occur within the regular classroom or outside of the regular classroom (pull-out).
key_sources: Corrective Reading. (2021). https://www.evidenceforessa.org/

article_title: Once Early-Reading Program
citation: Once Early-Reading Program: Evidence Rating Summary. (2025). https://once.org
title: Pair scripted tutoring delivered by non-specialist staff with weekly coaching based on session recordings and real-time progress data
description: The Once model makes non-specialist delivery viable by combining scripted, laptop-delivered lessons with a structured coaching loop: tutors receive weekly 30-minute coaching sessions from a consistent coach who reviews session recordings and provides targeted feedback, and a real-time data portal lets tutors, coaches, and administrators monitor student progress. This allows "staff without specialized reading instruction backgrounds to deliver sequenced lessons with fidelity". The article presents this staffing and supervision structure as integral to implementation.
requirements: A two-day, in-person training focused on the Science of Reading, the Once delivery method and model, and the Once technology, with ample time allocated for hands-on practice.
Weekly 30-minute coaching sessions from a consistent coach, plus laptop and internet access with a front-facing camera for session recording.
constraints: Coaching and data monitoring are described as components of the Once program specifically; the article does not report separate effects for the coaching component.
target_learners: PreK through first grade students receiving supplemental literacy tutoring
target_learning_goals: Early literacy skills delivered with fidelity by staff without specialized reading instruction backgrounds
examples: Tutors receive weekly 30-minute coaching sessions from a consistent Once coach who reviews session recordings and provides targeted feedback; a real-time data portal allows tutors, coaches, and administrators to monitor student progress.
key_sources: Once Early-Reading Program: Evidence Rating Summary. (2025). https://evidenceforessa.org/program/once-early-reading-program/

article_title: Building Assets Reducing Risks (BARR) — Attendance
citation: Building Assets Reducing Risks (BARR) program evidence summary. (2020). https://www.barrcenter.org
title: Sustain model implementation with multi-year sequenced professional development plus ongoing dedicated coaching
description: BARR pairs annual in-person training with continuous coaching: each school receives "two days of in-person professional development annually delivered through a sequenced, multi-year training plan," and "an average of more than 200 hours per year of personalized coaching and technical assistance." Year 1 training focuses on implementing the model; Years 2 and 3 address advanced topics such as effective team meetings, understanding trauma, reducing risky behaviors, and fostering student resilience.
requirements: A dedicated BARR coach assigned to each school providing structured weekly coaching sessions and quarterly on-site visits.
A sequenced, multi-year training plan using BARR materials and practice.
target_learners: teachers and school leaders implementing BARR
target_learning_goals: faithful implementation of the BARR model
examples: BARR coordinators and administrators also join quarterly Professional Learning Community calls and attend the annual BARR National Conference.
key_sources: Building Assets Reducing Risks (BARR) program evidence summary. (2020). https://evidenceforessa.org/program/building-assets-reducing-risks-barr-attendance/

article_title: Targeted Skills Instruction (TSI)
citation: Targeted Skills Instruction Evidence Rating Review. (2025). https://www.edmentum.com
title: Gradual release session structure for small-group tutoring: direct instruction, guided practice, independent work
description: Each TSI session follows "a gradual release model of direct instruction, collaborative, guided practice and independent work with tutor support." This structures each 30-45 minute tutoring session so responsibility shifts from tutor-led instruction to collaborative and guided practice and finally independent work, with the tutor available throughout. The pattern was implemented in every session of the studied program.
requirements: A tutor supporting each phase of the session
short sessions of 30-45 minutes repeated three or more times per week
target_learners: K-12 students in small tutoring groups of 2-6
examples: TSI sessions in the New Jersey study ran three 30-40 minute sessions per week following this structure
key_sources: Targeted Skills Instruction Evidence Rating Review. (2025). https://www.edmentum.com

article_title: STEMscopes Math
citation: STEMscopes Math Evidence Summary. (2024).
title: 5E+IA instructional model with Concrete-Representational-Abstract progression
description: The program's organizing instructional pattern is the 5E+IA model: "Engage, Explore, Explain, Elaborate, Evaluate, plus Intervention and Acceleration pathways." It structures whole-group instruction, small-group differentiation, and blended learning, and follows a "Concrete-Representational-Abstract progression" that sequences mathematical representations from concrete materials to abstract symbols, with digital tools such as virtual manipulatives and PhET simulations integrated.
requirements: Digital access devices for teachers and students to use the integrated digital tools
target_learning_goals: Mathematics concept and skill development across representational levels
examples: The curriculum embeds Intervention and Acceleration pathways alongside the five E phases
key_sources: STEMscopes Math Evidence Summary. (2024). https://evidenceforessa.org/program/stemscopes-math-2/

article_title: GO Tutor Corps High-Impact Math Tutoring
citation: GO Tutor Corps (Evidence Rating: Promising). (2024). GO Tutor Corps evidence summary. https://www.evidenceforessl.org/
title: Supplement classroom instruction with consistent in-school tutoring sessions that use student performance data to guide instruction
description: The article describes a tutoring model in which sessions occur during the school day, are consistent across the year, and use "student performance data to guide instruction." Tutoring is intended to supplement, not replace, regular classroom instruction, with progress monitoring tracking student progress over the school year.
requirements: A designated non-teaching staff member to manage tutors on-site during serving hours.
constraints: The evidence base is a single quasi-experimental study rated Promising, with a small +0.10 effect size.
target_learners: Students identified as needing additional help in mathematics
target_learning_goals: Improving mathematics achievement over the school year
examples: GO Tutor Corps delivered individualized or small-group math tutoring during the school day in participating schools, with progress monitoring across the year.
key_sources: GO Tutor Corps (Evidence Rating: Promising). (2024). GO Tutor Corps evidence summary. https://www.evidenceforessl.org/

article_title: Simple Solutions Learning – Standards-Based Math
citation: Simple Solutions Learning. (2025). Simple Solutions Learning evidence rating. https://www.simplesolutions.com
title: Supplement core instruction with short daily distributed review of previously taught skills to promote cumulative learning and retention
description: The article describes a design in which short, standards-aligned lessons revisit previously taught skills so that "the program's spiral structure is designed to strengthen recall and reduce learning loss by continually reintroducing previously covered content". Daily review of ten to fifteen problems in 10–15 minutes supplements, rather than replaces, the core curriculum. The evaluation associates this design with significantly greater assessment gains.
requirements: Daily implementation alongside the core math curriculum; teacher onboarding through professional development.
constraints: Evidence comes from one quasi-experimental study in grades 3–5; the design intent (retention, reduced learning loss) is stated by the program rather than separately tested.
target_learning_goals: Retention of previously taught math skills, procedural fluency, and multi-step reasoning
examples: Students completed ten to fifteen review problems per day, about 10–15 minutes, revisiting previously covered content.
key_sources: Simple Solutions Learning. (2025). Simple Solutions Learning evidence rating. https://www.simplesolutions.com

article_title: Waterford Upstart
citation: Waterford Upstart program description. (2024). https://www.waterford.org/upstart/
title: Pair home-based adaptive learning software with family coaching and progress updates
description: The program pairs its software with structured family involvement: "Each family is also assigned a coach who provides onboarding, routine-building guidance, and ongoing check-ins throughout the program period." Families also receive "weekly progress updates, simple at-home learning tips, and access to a bilingual resource library (English/Spanish) to help reinforce skills offline," supporting consistent use in home settings.
requirements: Assignment of a coach to each family for onboarding and ongoing check-ins
Weekly progress updates and at-home learning tips for families
constraints: Designed for home implementation by families of young children, not classroom-only delivery
target_learners: Children in PreK–2 and their families
target_learning_goals: Consistent daily engagement with early literacy, math, and science lessons
examples: Families receive weekly progress updates and use a bilingual English/Spanish resource library to reinforce skills offline

article_title: Waterford Upstart
citation: Waterford Upstart program description. (2024). https://www.waterford.org/upstart/
title: Short daily adaptive home-learning sessions sustained across the week
description: The program's usage pattern is short, frequent sessions: it "delivers daily 15–20 minute online lessons" and is "designed to be used consistently throughout the week," while the software "adjusts the level of support and difficulty as children demonstrate new skills." This combines brief session length, weekly regularity, and adaptive difficulty adjustment for young learners at home.

Family support to maintain consistent weekly use

article_title: STEMscopes Science
citation: STEMscopes evidence rating summary. (2024). Evidence rating: promising. https://www.stemscopes.com
title: 5E-based inquiry curriculum design with embedded formative assessment
description: The curriculum is organized around the 5E instructional model (Engage, Explore, Explain, Elaborate, Evaluate), pairing hands-on, inquiry-based investigations with real-world problem solving and embedded formative assessments. The article states the program is "grounded in the 5E instructional model" and is "designed to promote student engagement through interactive investigations, real-world problem solving, and embedded formative assessments."
requirements: Digital and print resources plus hands-on materials to support science instruction
constraints: Aligned to state standards, as evaluated in a Grade 5 science context
target_learning_goals: Science conceptual understanding and engagement through inquiry
examples: STEMscopes implements this pattern with interactive investigations and embedded formative assessments across digital, print, and hands-on materials.

article_title: STEMscopes Science
citation: STEMscopes evidence rating summary. (2024). Evidence rating: promising. https://www.stemscopes.com
title: Pair digital science curricula with hands-on materials to support instruction across diverse classrooms
description: The article recommends that a digital science curriculum should not be screen-only: STEMscopes "includes digital and print resources as well as hands-on materials to support science instruction across diverse classrooms." Combining a digital platform students can access via computer or touch screen device with physical investigation materials is presented as the way the program supports varied classroom contexts.

constraints: Evaluated in an urban district Grade 5 science setting

article_title: Twig Science
citation: Twig Science — Evidence Rating: Promising. (2025). Imagine Learning program evidence summary. https://www.imaginelearning.com
title: 5E instructional model structure (Engage, Explore, Explain, Elaborate, Evaluate) as the organizing lesson pattern
description: Twig Science organizes instruction around the 5E model, which the summary spells out as "Engage, Explore, Explain, Elaborate, Evaluate." Within this structure the curriculum places student inquiry at the center, embeds science and engineering practices, and sequences multimedia-rich investigations and collaborative tasks across the phases. Built-in literacy supports are integrated rather than treated separately.
requirements: Implementation in each classroom by one instructional teacher, with optional curriculum training varying by grade level.
constraints: Alignment is stated for the Next Generation Science Standards; no other standards alignment is claimed.
examples: The curriculum's investigations and collaborative tasks are delivered through the 5E phases across Grades K–8.

article_title: Progress Learning – Science
citation: Progress Learning evidence summary. (2024). Progress Learning (Evidence Rating: Promising). https://www.progresslearning.com/
title: Diagnostic-driven individualized learning paths with progress monitoring and dashboards
description: The program's instructional design pattern assigns every student a learning path or plan featuring specific standards aligned to individual learning needs. Diagnostics and progress monitoring help educators identify students not performing at grade level so they can provide resources to catch up, while district and school dashboards let teachers monitor progress across subjects and grade levels and identify trends that may inform curriculum and teaching strategies.
requirements: Teachers create and share assessments and assignments and track progress through the platform
target_learners: K-12 students needing grade-level remediation or standards-aligned practice
target_learning_goals: Closing gaps for students not performing at grade level
examples: Diagnostics and progress monitoring used in Forney ISD to identify students not performing at grade level

article_title: NEW INSIGHTS into Children’s Temperament (INSIGHTS) – Family Engagement
citation: INSIGHTS into Children's Temperament. (2010). Program description and evidence summary. https://www.evidencebasedprograms.org/programs/insights-into-childrens-temperament/
title: Align educator professional development, classroom sessions, and parent education around a shared temperament framework
description: INSIGHTS works by giving the adults around the child a common framework: educators and parents each receive six self-paced lessons followed by remote facilitated sessions that help them "recognize their children's temperaments/personalities and learn strategies to reduce behavior problems and enhance social skills," while classroom sessions teach children the same temperament ideas. The article presents this three-component alignment as the program's design for improving self-regulation, classroom engagement, and teacher-student relationships.
requirements: Educators and parents complete six one-hour asynchronized and six one-hour synchronized lessons
target_learners: early elementary students and the teachers and families who support them
examples: The trial delivered the program simultaneously to students, teachers, and parents over ten weekly sessions.

article_title: I CAN Learn® Primary Mathematics
citation: What Works Clearinghouse, Institute of Education Sciences, U.S. Department of Education. (2017, July). Primary Mathematics intervention report: I CAN Learn®. Retrieved from https://whatworks.ed.gov
title: Five-part self-paced mastery lesson structure
description: I CAN Learn® lessons follow a repeating five-part design in which instruction is delivered by software and advancement is gated by demonstrated mastery. The curriculum studied included "109 lessons, each of which has a five-part format that includes a warm-up activity, lesson presentation, journal activity, guided practice, and a quiz to ensure mastery of the lesson content". Students complete lessons individually at their own pace using interactive software with a virtual teacher that presents multimodal lessons and demonstrates problem solving when students make errors, while the classroom teacher supports students with the lessons.
requirements: Computer equipment, desks, and electrical connectivity in classrooms; the developer provided maintenance and technical and instructional support to teachers
constraints: The study did not specify which edition of the curriculum was used
examples: In the reviewed quasi-experiment, intervention students used this lesson format as the primary source of math instruction for the entire academic school year in 12 to 14 middle schools

article_title: Headsprout® Early Reading
citation: What Works Clearinghouse, U.S. Department of Education. (2009). Headsprout® Early Reading (WWC Intervention Report). http://www.headsprout.com/
title: Adaptive computer-assisted early literacy pattern: adaptive instruction with performance criteria, cumulative review, and printable reinforcement materials
description: The program's instructional design combines several recurring features: the curriculum "provides individualized, adaptive instruction", responds "to a child's pattern of errors with tutorials and reviews to provide extra assistance", requires that "children must meet specific performance criteria in order to progress", builds in "cumulative review ... to help ensure retention", and pairs episodes with printed Readers whose "stories only contain material that children have learned up to that point". Teachers receive generated performance reports to monitor progress.
requirements: Computers must be available to children (a mobile computer lab in the study)
Teachers trained to respond to technology issues, access and decipher reports, and redirect students when necessary

target_learning_goals: early literacy skills: phonemic awareness, phonics, fluency, vocabulary, comprehension
examples: Children use the mouse to navigate episodes, for example helping a worm get home by identifying, from among four pairs of letters, the letters that represent a sound they learned

article_title: Pre-K Mathematics
citation: What Works Clearinghouse, Institute of Education Sciences, U.S. Department of Education. (2023, September). Pre-K Mathematics. https://whatworks.ed.gov
title: Linked classroom and home caregiver-child math activity model for early mathematics
description: This instructional pattern pairs weekly teacher-led small-group classroom math activities with caregiver-child home activities linked to the classroom content. Each classroom activity includes "a core lesson as well as additional activities to tailor the lesson for lower- and higher-performing children" and scaffolding suggestions for common errors. Home packets contain the activity, manipulatives, and a bilingual caregiver letter with a picture strip depicting how to conduct the activity.
requirements: Teacher training in implementing the curriculum with fidelity and in progress monitoring, plus ongoing in-class coaching
constraints: Implemented in Head Start and state-funded preschool settings with low-income families; effects on non-mathematics domains were uncertain

target_learning_goals: early mathematics achievement and informal mathematical knowledge

article_title: Reading Mastery
citation: What Works Clearinghouse, U.S. Department of Education. (2010). WWC Intervention Report: Reading Mastery (Adolescent Literacy). http://www.mcgraw-hill.co.uk/sra/downloads/Reading%20Mastery/Reading%20Mastery%20Signature%20Edition%20Brochure.pdf
title: Reading Mastery lesson pattern: modeling, guided practice, and individual practice within scripted 30–45 minute multi-strand lessons
description: A typical Reading Mastery lesson lasts 30 to 45 minutes and includes "seven to nine short activities that encompass multiple strands of content, such as phonemic awareness, letter-sound correspondence, sounding out words, word recognition, vocabulary, oral reading fluency, or comprehension." The repeated teaching routine proceeds through modeling new content, providing guided practice, and implementing individual practice and application. Lesson scripts guide teachers, and signals and group responses keep students involved and on task while controlling lesson pacing.
requirements: Lesson scripts act as a guide for teachers
Signals and group responses are used to keep students involved and on task, and to control lesson pacing
target_learners: Elementary students in grades K–6, including struggling readers

examples: The program typically spans one academic year with daily lessons of this structure

article_title: Core-Plus Mathematics
citation: Core-Plus Mathematics. (2010). WWC Intervention Report: Core-Plus Mathematics, High School Math. What Works Clearinghouse, U.S. Department of Education. http://www.wmich.edu/cpmp
title: Core-Plus multi-day lesson cycle: launch, small-group investigation, Checkpoint discussion, and independent task
description: Core-Plus units are organized around multi-day lessons cycling through instructional activities: a full-class launch of a problem situation with the teacher as "director and moderator"; small-group investigation in which students gather data, look for patterns, construct models, and make and verify conjectures with the teacher as facilitator; a whole-class Checkpoint discussion with the teacher as moderator; and an individual task with the teacher as "an intellectual coach". Materials promote collaborative small-group investigations followed by teacher-led whole-class summarizing that leads to analysis, abstraction, and further application.
requirements: Classroom configurations supporting small-group work in class and individual work outside class, with teacher roles shifting across director, facilitator, moderator, and coach
constraints: The cycle is described for the first edition of the curriculum reviewed by the WWC
target_learning_goals: Mathematical thinking, problem solving, and conceptual understanding through investigation of problem situations
examples: Lessons begin with a full-class discussion of a problem situation, then shift to investigating focused problems by gathering data, looking for patterns, constructing models and meanings, and making and verifying conjectures
key_sources: Core-Plus Mathematics. (2010). WWC Intervention Report: Core-Plus Mathematics, High School Math. What Works Clearinghouse, U.S. Department of Education. http://www.wmich.edu/cpmp

article_title: Sound Partners
citation: Sound Partners. (2010). WWC Intervention Report: Sound Partners. What Works Clearinghouse, U.S. Department of Education. http://www.wri-edu.org/partners/sound-partners.htm
title: Short frequent one-to-one tutoring sessions with scripted phonics lessons and mastery checks
description: The program's instructional pattern is "30 minute sessions of one-to-one tutoring that take place four days per week throughout one school year." Each session includes from four to eight short activities, with the last 15 minutes allocated for oral reading practice in decodable texts matched to taught phonics skills. Although scripted, instruction can be adjusted to individual student needs, and tests given every 10 lessons gauge student mastery.
requirements: Tutors trained to choose a reading method (independent reading, partner reading, or echo reading) matching each student's reading skills
constraints: Tutoring is supplemental; treatment students in the reviewed studies also received typical classroom reading instruction
target_learners: Kindergarten and first-grade students at risk for reading difficulties
target_learning_goals: Applying word-level phonics skills in oral text reading
examples: In Vadasy and Sanders (2008), tutoring for both treatment groups occurred in 30-minute sessions, four days per week, for 18 weeks, one-on-one or in pairs.

article_title: Spalding’s The Writing Road to Reading
citation: Spalding's The Writing Road to Reading. (2024). Program description and evidence review. https://evidenceforesc.org/
title: Build in-house certified trainers to sustain program expertise within the school

This makes ongoing coaching and fidelity monitoring locally sustainable.

A coordinator role to oversee fidelity and provide coaching

article_title: EveryDay Intervention (Family Engagement)
citation: Attendance. (2018). https://www.evidenceforlearning.org
title: Attendance interventions can be delivered at scale with minimal staffing, training, and technology
description: The page specifies that the Absence Reports intervention requires minimal staffing — one district staff member supporting implementation at approximately 30 minutes per week and one district-level data staff member supporting data transfer in under 3 hours total — and that professional development is minimal, with "none required aside from the staffing requirements described above," and no technology required. This shows a low-burden delivery model can accompany a statistically significant attendance effect, making district adoption feasible without extensive training infrastructure.

constraints: Staffing estimates are as printed for this program; the page does not generalize them to other interventions

target_learning_goals: Reducing student absences through feasible district-level implementation

article_title: PowerSchool Attendance Intervention (Family Engagement)
citation: PowerSchool Attendance Intervention. (2024). PowerSchool Attendance Intervention program description and evidence summary. https://www.powerschool.com/
title: Teacher-mediated automated attendance messaging pattern combining dashboards, templates, and two-way family communication
description: The intervention operationalizes attendance improvement as a teacher-family communication workflow: educators monitor daily and period-level attendance and chronic absenteeism data, then use customized messaging templates with automatically populated parent or student names and real-time attendance data, delivered via two-way texting and email. Auto-translation features help administrators and treatment teachers reach parents from diverse backgrounds. This pattern reduces the time burden for school staff while keeping communication personalized and data-driven.
requirements: Access to a school or district administrative system to gather attendance data
Teachers and administrators trained via the Train-the-Trainer methodology
constraints: Effectiveness evidence comes from a semester-long RCT in 3 DC public schools with 6th-12th grade students; in-seat attendance effects were insignificant.
examples: Teachers in the treatment condition used the app and training to communicate with families, while control teachers communicated with parents as usual.

article_title: Flashlight360
citation: Flashlight360 program description. (2024). https://flashlight360.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/23505832409499-Device-Specifications
title: Deliver actionable language data so teachers can offer constructive feedback that accelerates language development
description: The article states that "By delivering actionable data, Flashlight360 supports teachers in offering constructive feedback, a proven approach to accelerating language development." The principle is that progress-monitoring tools should give teachers actionable data on specific language areas so feedback can be focused and meaningful for both teachers and students working toward proficiency.
requirements: Scoring and feedback across defined language areas (five speaking areas, three writing areas) so feedback can be targeted
examples: Flashlight360 delivers scoring and feedback across five areas of speaking and three areas of writing to guide teacher and student efforts toward proficiency.

article_title: Renzulli Learning

title: Differentiate instruction by focusing on individual student strengths and interests to foster engagement

The principle is to personalize learning around each student's strengths and interests as a route to engagement.

article_title: OnYourMark

title: Pair students with a consistent tutor at a small student-tutor ratio to build positive tutoring relationships
description: The program builds positive tutor-student relationships by keeping the student-tutor ratio small and "pairing students with a consistent tutor for the duration of the program". Relationship-building is treated as part of effective delivery, alongside content knowledge, in tutors' ongoing professional development.
requirements: Tutors receive initial training and ongoing professional development focused on content knowledge, building relationships, and effective delivery of the intervention

article_title: BookNook
citation: BookNook: Evidence Rating Strong. (2023). https://www.booknook.org
title: Keep the same tutor and small student group together so the tutor can learn each student's strengths and skill gaps
description: BookNook assigns students so that "students meet with the same tutor and small group of students to build relationships and to facilitate the tutor to develop an understanding of each student's strengths and skill gaps." The principle is that tutor-student consistency and small grouping serve relationship-building and diagnostic knowledge, which the program treats as integral to tutoring effectiveness.

constraints: The page asserts this design rationale without reporting a separate test of the consistency mechanism itself

examples: BookNook's model pairs each small group with one tutor across the program's 12-week, multi-session schedule.

article_title: Hoot Reading – MTSS Tier III
citation: Hoot Reading — Evidence Summary. (2025). https://www.hootreading.com

This design allows virtual one-to-one tutoring to run within schools without specialized hardware, with school staff supervising at each location while tutors are provided by the program.

A web application accessible via an internet browser

article_title: Progress Learning – Math

title: Use diagnostics and progress monitoring to identify students below grade level and assign targeted resources
description: The article describes Progress Learning's diagnostics and progress monitoring as the mechanism for catching students up: "Diagnostics and progress monitoring help educators understand which students are not performing at grade level so that they can provide the resources they need to catch up." Dashboards for school- and district-level monitoring

article_title: Progress Learning – Reading

description: The program embeds diagnostics and progress monitoring so educators can see which students are behind. article_title: Scholastic RISE and RISE Up
citation: Schechter et al. (2024). Scholastic RISE and RISE Up program evaluation, Florida district, 2022-2023 school year.
title: Small-group station rotation for Tier 2 reading intervention
description: The program organizes intervention as rotation of small groups of four students through instructional stations. In RISE, "groups of four students rotate through four instruction stations for 45-60 minutes per day for six to eight weeks"; RISE Up uses three stations focused on comprehension strategies on a short text for 45 minutes a day. The rotation distributes explicit, structured instruction across comprehension, word study, phonics, and writing.

45-60 minutes per day
Six to eight weeks of implementation
Teacher(s) or interventionists staffing the stations

article_title: Parent Teacher Home Visits – Attendance
citation: Parent Teacher Home Visits. (2021). Evidence summary reporting a 2021 Mathematica Regional Educational Laboratory Mid-Atlantic quasi-experimental study. https://www.mathematica.org
title: PTHV five non-negotiables for relationship-building home visits
description: The PTHV model specifies five non-negotiable design features: "Visits are voluntary and arranged in advance"; "Teachers are trained and compensated for visits"; "Visits focus on hopes and dreams"; "Educators visit a cross-section of students (not a targeted intervention)"; and "Educators go in pairs and reflect." These features define how the program is implemented as a universal rather than targeted family engagement practice.

constraints: The model is explicitly not a targeted intervention; educators visit a cross-section of students

article_title: Strategic Adolescent Reading Intervention (STARI)
citation: Strategic Adolescent Reading Intervention (STARI) program evidence summary. (2024). Evidence for ESSA. https://www.evidenceforessa.org
title: Four types of peer collaboration embedded in a reading intervention
description: STARI was designed to promote social interactions that foster student engagement, structuring peer collaboration in four recurring formats across its units. The program "uses four types of peer collaboration: partner-assisted fluency practice, reciprocal teaching of comprehension strategies, partner reading and responding to novels and nonfiction texts, and peer debate, in which teams gather text evidence and build arguments." Peer contexts also push students to articulate personal stances on texts and compare them with partners or classmates.
requirements: Trained teachers able to facilitate discussion and build a strong classroom culture
constraints: Implemented within the STARI curriculum's thematic units for struggling middle school readers
target_learners: middle school students who struggle with reading
examples: Peer debate teams gather text evidence and build arguments; partners read and respond to novels and nonfiction texts
key_sources: Strategic Adolescent Reading Intervention (STARI) program evidence summary. (2024). Evidence for ESSA. https://evidenceforessa.org/program/strategic-adolescent-reading-intervention-stari/

article_title: Strategic Adolescent Reading Intervention (STARI)

title: Staff STARI with trained teachers who facilitate discussion and build classroom culture, not necessarily reading specialists

"STARI is a teacher-led program, and the program’s success relies on the teacher’s ability to facilitate discussion and build a strong classroom culture." Because the curriculum is clearly laid out and professional learning is comprehensive, teachers from a variety of backgrounds have demonstrated success, and a licensed reading specialist is not necessary.
requirements: Teachers trained to implement STARI, able to facilitate discussion and build a strong classroom culture
constraints: A licensed reading specialist is not necessary; success depends on facilitation ability
target_learners: middle school students who struggle with reading
target_learning_goals: reading comprehension and component reading skills
examples: Certified teachers recruited from participating schools received training during a 3-day summer institute and feedback from literacy coaches throughout the intervention

Completion of the program's instructor-led training (two hours in the study)

article_title: Collaborative Strategic Reading (CSR)
citation: Collaborative Strategic Reading. (2024). Evidence for Impact. https://www.evidenceforimpact.org
title: Pair initial CSR training with ongoing booster sessions and in-school coaching for teachers

This initial training is followed by "Four 2-hour follow-up booster sessions" recommended throughout the school year, plus individual coaching and support for school-based teams and literacy coaches.
requirements: Two days of initial professional development covering the core CSR components
Four 2-hour follow-up booster sessions across the school year
target_learning_goals: teacher ability to teach the core components of CSR
examples: Individual coaching and support for school-based teams and literacy coaches is also available.

article_title: Talent Development High School (TDHS) — Strategic Reading and Student Team Literature
citation: Talent Development High School. (2004). Talent Development High School program description and evidence review. https://www.bestevidence.org
title: Double-dose semester block: Strategic Reading first semester, English 1 second semester
description: TDHS gives ninth graders a double dose of reading: students take double periods of Strategic Reading, 90 minutes daily, in the first semester, and then double periods of English 1 in the second semester. This sequencing concentrates intensive reading instruction before the standard English course. The pattern is the structural backbone of the reading component of the whole-school model.
requirements: Scheduling capacity for 90-minute daily double reading periods in the first semester
constraints: Applies to ninth graders in high-poverty schools as implemented in the qualifying study
target_learners: Ninth graders in high-poverty high schools
examples: Double periods of Strategic Reading (90 minutes daily) in the first semester, then double periods of English 1 in the second semester

article_title: Talent Development High School (TDHS) — Strategic Reading and Student Team Literature
citation: Talent Development High School. (2004). Talent Development High School program description and evidence review. https://www.bestevidence.org
title: Cooperative learning groups with paired reading, vocabulary practice, and structured partner discussion guides
description: In Strategic Reading, students work in small, interdependent cooperative learning groups. Activities include paired reading for fluency and comprehension, practice with new vocabulary related to novels and plays, and structured partner discussion guides that provide background, vocabulary, and comprehension questions to help students identify characters, plots, and informational content. Students also get time for self-selected reading and writing activities.
requirements: Structured partner discussion guides providing background, vocabulary, and comprehension questions
High-quality student materials, which teachers unanimously rated highly in the implementation survey
target_learners: Ninth graders in high-poverty high schools
target_learning_goals: Comprehension of characters, plots, and informational content
examples: Paired reading for fluency and comprehension; mini-lessons on specific comprehension strategies; self-selected reading and writing activities
key_sources: Talent Development High School. (2004). Talent Development High School program description and evidence review. https://www.bestevidence.org

article_title: Talent Development High School (TDHS) — Strategic Reading and Student Team Literature
citation: Talent Development High School. (2004). Talent Development High School program description and evidence review. https://www.bestevidence.org
title: Support whole-school reading reform with sustained job-embedded coaching rather than one-off training
description: The program's implementation model pairs brief start-up training with sustained job-embedded support: two days of start-up and awareness training for all Strategic Reading teachers, plus two days per month of job-embedded JHU Instructional Facilitator support, within roughly 20 days of facilitator support overall. A minimum of 3 days of technical assistance from a JHU ELA facilitator is required. Teachers rated the in-class assistance and workshop training highly.
requirements: One FTE English teacher per cohort of 75-100 students; an English Instructional Coach if possible
constraints: A minimum of 3 days of technical assistance from a JHU ELA facilitator is required
target_learners: Ninth graders in high-poverty high schools
target_learning_goals: Reading comprehension and fluency through well-implemented Strategic Reading
examples: Two days per month of job-embedded JHU Instructional Facilitator support during 2002-2003 implementation

article_title: Classworks Math
citation: Classworks Individualized Learning. (2022). Evidence summary. https://www.classworks.com
title: Teachers should actively monitor progress and reassign assignments to support mastery in individualized learning programs
description: The summary presents teacher monitoring as essential to realizing the program's benefit: "To ensure the optimal impact of Classworks Individualized Learning, it is essential for teachers to actively monitor student progress and reassign assignments as needed to support student mastery." Individualized paths only produce learning when adults track progress and adjust assignments rather than letting the software run unattended.
requirements: Teachers have access to student progress data and the ability to reassign instructional units
target_learners: Students using individualized online intervention units
examples: Classworks implementation guidance directs teachers to monitor progress and reassign assignments as needed during use of Individualized Learning Paths
key_sources: Classworks Individualized Learning. (2022). Evidence summary. https://www.classworks.com

article_title: Classworks Math
citation: Classworks Individualized Learning. (2022). Evidence summary. https://www.classworks.com
title: Individualized learning unit pattern: direct instruction, applied activities, and formative mastery check
description: Each Classworks instructional unit follows a recurring structure: "direct instruction, activities to apply learning, and a short formative test focused on strengthening a specific skill." Direct instruction comes in two-to-three-minute segments teachers can also use in classrooms, extended learning takes the form of interactive games and activities that differentiate by instructional strategies, and a formative assessment confirms mastery. Students encounter varied instructional approaches, interactivity types, and degrees of games versus concrete instruction as they learn each skill.
requirements: Assessment data from which to generate the Individualized Learning Path
constraints: Units target one specific skill at a time
examples: Classworks units pair two-to-three-minute direct-instruction segments with interactive games and a short formative test per skill
key_sources: Classworks Individualized Learning. (2022). Evidence summary. https://www.classworks.com

article_title: Journeys
citation: Houghton Mifflin Harcourt Journeys: Evidence Review. (2017). https://www.hmhco.com/programs/journeys
title: Whole-group introduction followed by small-group homogeneous practice of the same skills
description: The Journeys program organizes daily literacy instruction in two tiers: whole group activities introduce a "big idea" and "essential question" for the day, a teacher read-aloud, and vocabulary, phonics, comprehension, and fluency activities. Small group activities then "follow up these same skills in small, homogeneous groups," so all students meet the same content with differentiated group support.
requirements: Grade-level classroom teacher guiding whole-group, small-group, and independent sessions
constraints: Evaluated only in grades K-2
examples: Small group activities follow up the same skills introduced in whole group instruction in small, homogeneous groups.
key_sources: Houghton Mifflin Harcourt Journeys: Evidence Review. (2017). https://www.hmhco.com/programs/journeys

article_title: Future Forward Literacy
citation: Future Forward: Evidence Rating Strong program description. (2022). https://www.evidenceforlearners.org/future-forward
title: School-community-family partnership pattern pairing tutoring dosage with regular family contact
description: The program's design pattern combines a minimum tutoring dosage with structured family outreach: "FF sites are expected to provide students with a minimum of three 30-minute tutoring sessions per week and to communicate with families at least two times per month." Tutoring is individualized, with sessions varying "based on the skills and interests of the students," while the family engagement coordinator runs monthly family events and ongoing contacts to support literacy development outside school.

A family engagement coordinator for family outreach and communication
Generally paraprofessional tutors conducting one-on-one sessions
constraints: The pattern was evaluated with mixed results under disrupted conditions: the COVID-19-modified version yielded a non-significant effect of +0.09
target_learners: Elementary students (K-3) struggling with reading in low-income school communities
target_learning_goals: Foundational literacy skills including phonological awareness, reading, and writing
examples: Monthly family events and ongoing contacts facilitate literacy development outside of school while tutors deliver individualized sessions focused on letter sounds, shared readings, and writing activities

article_title: Leveled Literacy Intervention (LLI)
citation: Leveled Literacy Intervention (LLI) evidence summary. (2010). Evidence review of two qualifying studies. https://www.heinemann.com
title: Alternating independent-level and instructional-level texts across tutoring lessons
description: Within LLI, lessons alternate between "independent level" texts and more challenging "instructional level" texts. The instructional-level texts may also be taken back to students' classrooms or homes, extending the tutoring texts into classroom and home reading.
requirements: A supply of leveled texts at both independent and instructional levels for each student
constraints: Applied within a small-group tutoring model for early-grade struggling readers
target_learning_goals: reading fluency and comprehension at increasing text difficulty
examples: LLI lessons alternate the two text levels across the 16-18 week tutoring period

article_title: REDI (Research-Based, Developmentally Informed)
citation: REDI (Research Based, Developmentally Informed). (2024). Program description page, Evidence Rating: promising. http://www.pathseducation.com/
title: Pairing social-emotional learning with interactive storybook reading and phonological awareness activities in preschool
description: REDI's instructional design combines an SEL curriculum with structured early-literacy activities: "an interactive storybook reading and retelling approach, along with phonological awareness training and alphabet center activities." The pattern pairs self-regulation and emotional-control teaching with language and print activities in the same preschool day.

article_title: Every Classroom, Every Day (ECED) — Reading
citation: Every Classroom, Every Day (ECED). (2019). Evidence for ESSA program review. https://www.evidenceforessa.org
title: Designate an on-site instructional coach to monitor and support ECED implementation
description: ECED's staffing requirements state that implementation "Requires a designated on-site instructional coach or leader to monitor and support implementation", noting "This position may look different depending on size of school". Both curricula also "require a reallocation of existing school staff to teach each of the courses". The coach role is part of the program's implementation model rather than an evaluated manipulation in the outcome study.
requirements: A designated on-site instructional coach or leader
Reallocation of existing school staff to teach the courses
constraints: The position may look different depending on size of school
target_learners: high school students in ECED schools
target_learning_goals: literacy and math achievement through faithful program implementation

article_title: Every Classroom, Every Day (ECED) — Reading
citation: Every Classroom, Every Day (ECED). (2019). Evidence for ESSA program review. https://www.evidenceforessa.org
title: ECED professional development model: institute, site visits, and monthly check-ins across two years
description: ECED's professional development combines an initial institute, recurring on-site visits, and regular remote check-ins. "Both years include: Three-day institute for teachers (introductory/reflection, pace support, strategy and lesson modeling)" and "Four 3-day site visits per year (workshops, model lessons, strategies, individual and group coaching, class visits)", plus "Monthly phone check-ins". The second year of professional development is optional but recommended, making the model a sustained, coaching-based design rather than a one-off training.
requirements: Three-day teacher institute in each year
Four 3-day site visits per year
Monthly phone check-ins
constraints: The second year of professional development is optional, but recommended
target_learning_goals: implementing the ECED literacy curricula and Power 10 strategies with fidelity
examples: Site visits include workshops, model lessons, strategies, individual and group coaching, and class visits.

article_title: TalkingPoints
citation: Academic Performance. (2024). TalkingPoints. https://talkingpoints.org
title: Family engagement tools should require no additional staffing or PD to be usable at scale
description: The article presents TalkingPoints as implementable without burdening schools: "No additional staffing required" and "There are no PD or training requirements for use." Support is instead embedded, with individual teacher accounts receiving in-app coaching and guidance, and school or district accounts able to access additional guided implementation and PD if desired.
requirements: In-app coaching and guidance must be built into teacher, school, and district accounts
constraints: Guided implementation and PD beyond in-app coaching are optional add-ons rather than included requirements
examples: Individual teacher accounts come with in-app coaching and guidance; school and district accounts can add guided implementation and PD

article_title: Pathblazer
citation: Pathblazer evidence summary. (2020). https://www.edgenuity.com/support/technical-requirements/
title: Gradual release instructional model: explicit instruction, supported practice, independent practice, and assessments
description: All Pathblazer lessons in math and reading "are built around a gradual release instructional model of explicit instruction, supported practice, independent practice, and assessments." Each lesson moves responsibility from teacher-led explicit instruction to student independent work, with assessments embedded to check mastery. This structure underpins the individualized learning paths the program assigns to close identified skill and concept gaps.
requirements: Assessments embedded at the end of the lesson sequence to verify mastery
target_learners: struggling K–8 learners working to close skill and concept gaps

article_title: AARP Foundation Experience Corps Tutoring (Book Buddies)
citation: AARP Foundation Experience Corps. (2021). AARP Foundation Experience Corps. Evidence for ESSA program summary. https://www.evidenceforessa.org
title: Staff Experience Corps programs with a Project Director, Site Coordinators, and Volunteer Team Leaders
description: The page states that although staffing structure varies, "best practice indicates that programs with a Project Director, Site Coordinators, and Volunteer Team Leaders are the most successful". The Project Director oversees day-to-day operations; Site Coordinators maintain relationships with schools, principals, teachers, and volunteers and can manage up to 5 schools; Volunteer Team Leaders handle daily communication with and data collection from volunteers.
requirements: Number of Site Coordinators and Volunteer Team Leaders scaled to the number of volunteers and schools served
constraints: Site Coordinators can manage up to 5 schools with assistance from Volunteer Team Leaders

article_title: Reading Apprenticeship
citation: Reading Apprenticeship. (2024). Evidence for ESSA program review. https://www.evidenceforessa.org
title: Integrating metacognitive strategy instruction into content-area courses with collaborative sense-making
description: All Reading Apprenticeship variations share a common instructional design: they integrate metacognitive strategy instruction into subject-area teaching rather than a stand-alone reading curriculum. As the review states, the programs "incorporate extensive reading, collaborative sense-making, and teaching of meta-cognitive skills such as prediction, summarization, graphic organizers, and clarification." Teachers model reasoning processes so strategies are learned in the context of authentic content reading.
requirements: Teachers receive extensive professional development and coaching, including analyses of classroom video and modeling of reasoning processes
target_learners: high school students in science and social studies, including struggling readers
target_learning_goals: metacognitive reading strategies such as prediction, summarization, graphic organizers, and clarification

article_title: Early Literacy and Learning Model/Plus (ELLM/Plus)
citation: Early Literacy and Learning Model (ELLM/Plus). (2008). Evidence rating summary, Preschool Curriculum Evaluation Research (PCER) studies.
title: ELLM coaching cycle: coach models a lesson, teacher implements it, and written analysis of critical behaviors feeds a feedback and reflection conference
description: The ELLM coaching cycle addresses effective teaching skills for each literacy component and runs from coach modeling to the teacher assimilating critical behaviors into daily practice. The coach first models a lesson demonstrating desired instructional behaviors while the teacher conducts a written analysis; a feedback and reflection conference asks "What worked? What needs to be added? What needs to be extended?". In the next cycle the teacher implements the lesson while the coach observes and analyzes the teacher's critical behaviors, followed by another conference in which coach and teacher plan the next cycle. Critical behaviors are specified in advance and analyzed during delivery.
requirements: Literacy coaches trained via a five-day summer institute and weekly coaching seminars
Critical behaviors specified in advance and analyzed during delivery
constraints: Additional support beyond the cycle is delivered only through abbreviated coaching sessions, teacher observations, or instructional materials
target_learning_goals: Effective teaching skills and behaviors for each literacy component
examples: The first phase has the coach modeling the lesson while the teacher observes and conducts a written analysis

grain_size: lesson-level coaching cycle repeated across literacy components

article_title: Content-Focused Coaching — Whole Class
citation: Content-Focused Coaching. (2023). Content-Focused Coaching. Evidence for ESSA. https://www.evidenceforessa.org
title: Question-the-Author literacy pattern: students question texts and challenge each other's interpretations
description: The literacy strategies used in CFC are drawn from Question the Author: teachers pose questions to students to promote understanding, interpretation, and active response. Students are encouraged to challenge each other's interpretations and to challenge the authors, identifying places in texts where they want to know more. This pattern positions students as active interrogators of text meaning rather than passive recipients.
requirements: Teachers learn to pose questions to students to promote understanding, interpretation, and active response
target_learning_goals: Text understanding, interpretation, and active response
examples: Students identify places in texts in which they want to know more and challenge each other's interpretations during CFC-supported literacy lessons.

article_title: Literacy First – UT Austin
citation: Literacy First program description and evaluation summary. (2021). https://literacyfirst.org
title: Daily individualized tutoring sessions with response-to-intervention progress monitoring
description: The program's instructional design combines daily one-to-one tutoring with continuous data use. Tutors "work with their students daily in 30 minutes sessions that are tailored to address individual literacy/language needs," and the program is "data driven, with tutors using a response-to-intervention model that involves benchmark assessments and weekly progress monitoring." Attendance, fidelity, and implementation data are collected to inform both individualization and programmatic impact.
requirements: Trained tutors available daily for 30-minute sessions
Benchmark assessments and weekly progress monitoring instruments
constraints: Designed for students in kindergarten through grade 2 reading below grade level
target_learners: Struggling readers in kindergarten through grade 2
examples: Tutors use benchmark assessments and weekly progress monitoring to tailor sessions to individual literacy and language needs

article_title: Literacy First – UT Austin
citation: Literacy First program description and evaluation summary. (2021). https://literacyfirst.org
title: Invest in substantial tutor training and ongoing expert coaching to deliver one-to-one early literacy tutoring
description: The article presents extensive tutor preparation and continuous expert support as core to how the program operates: tutors "receive more than 70 hours of training in best practices and weekly visits from Literacy First experts and coaches," plus 70+ hours of training "on evidence-based best practices in early literacy instruction." This training and coaching infrastructure underpins the tutoring that produced the measured reading gains.
requirements: Full-time supervisors at a ratio of one per 20 full-time tutors across five campuses
constraints: Program is delivered in person; virtual training and professional support is available when needed
target_learners: Students in kindergarten through grade 2 reading below grade level
examples: Tutors received 70+ hours of training and weekly visits from program experts and coaches during the evaluated implementation

article_title: 95 Phonics Core Program
citation: 95 Phonics Core Program — Evidence Rating. (2024). https://www.95percentgroup.com
title: Structured scope-and-sequence lesson pattern with daily 20-30 minute explicit phonics instruction
description: The program organizes instruction around a scope and sequence of lessons per grade — 25 lessons for Kindergarten and 30 lessons for each of Grades 1-5. Each lesson "focuses on specific phonics skills, provides examples of high-frequency words, and contains information about other skills addressed within the topic," delivered in short daily sessions of 20-30 minutes.

article_title: Lenses on Literature — Evidence for ESSA
citation: Lenses on Literature. (2013). Lenses on Literature. https://www.literacydesigncollaborative.org
title: Sequenced literacy units organized around a Driving Task Prompt moving through comprehension, knowledge building, genre study, synthesis, and writing
description: This pattern organizes curriculum units and modules around a Driving Task Prompt within a disciplinary-literacy framework. Students explore complex, diverse texts through a sequenced instructional journey that includes comprehension, knowledge building, genre study, synthesis, and writing. The design purposefully builds knowledge and supports text-based analysis and communication across genres and formats.
requirements: Units require complex, diverse texts and standards-aligned rubrics for embedded formative assessment of performance tasks.
examples: Teachers implemented at least two Lenses modules in history/social studies or science in the Kentucky study.

article_title: Lenses on Literature — Evidence for ESSA
citation: Lenses on Literature. (2013). Lenses on Literature. https://www.literacydesigncollaborative.org
title: Use a digital platform to deliver layered scaffolding, differentiation, and ongoing formative assessment with standards-aligned rubrics
description: Lenses is a hybrid program with print and digital components. The digital platform ensures that teachers can deliver layers of scaffolding and differentiation to meet varied learning needs, conduct ongoing formative assessment, and use standards-aligned rubrics to score periodic and summative performance tasks. The principle is that technology should serve differentiation and formative assessment within daily instruction.
requirements: A hybrid print and digital program structure with standards-aligned rubrics from the Stanford Center for Assessment, Learning, and Equity.
target_learning_goals: formative assessment of reading and writing
examples: The program provides robust scaffolds for multilingual learners and embedded formative assessments using standards-aligned rubrics.

article_title: EveryDay Intervention (Formerly InClass Today and EveryDay Labs)
citation: EveryDay Intervention (formerly InClassToday) Absence Reports Intervention — Evidence Summary. (2018). https://www.everydaylabs.com
title: Deliver personalized attendance information directly to parents as a low-burden absenteeism intervention
description: The article's program model is that mailing parents "actionable, personalized information about their student's attendance" can change attendance behavior without instructional changes at school. Implementation burden is minimal: staffing is "one district staff member to support program implementation (approximately 30 min/week)" plus a data staff member, with no professional development, training, or technology required.

One district staff member (~30 min/week) and one district-level data staff member (< 3 hrs total)

target_learning_goals: Reducing absences so students attend and benefit from instruction

article_title: Early Warning Intervention and Monitoring System (EWIMS)
citation: Faria et al. (2017). Early Warning Intervention and Monitoring System (EWIMS). https://eric.ed.gov/?q=early+warning+intervention+and+monitoring+system

Data on attendance, suspensions, grades, and credits

article_title: Chapter One (Formerly Innovations for Learning High Impact Tutoring)
citation: Chapter One. (2024). Chapter One — Evidence Rating: Strong. https://www.evidenceforlearning.org/chapter-one

A student-relay handoff minimizes interruptions to classroom instruction.

article_title: Early Learning in Mathematics

article_title: Galaxy Math

description: Galaxy Math operationalizes tutoring as a scripted, fixed-dosage, one-to-one delivery model: "The program is scripted, and tutors are expected to follow the scripts without reading them or memorizing them." article_title: PowerSchool Attendance Intervention
citation: PowerSchool Attendance Intervention. (2024). Evidence for ESI program review. https://www.evidenceforessi.org/
title: Automate personalization of family communication templates to reduce staff time burden
description: The review states that "[t]he ability to automatically populate a parent or student's name and real-time attendance data into communication templates greatly reduces the time burden for school staff." requirements: Access to a school or district administrative system supplying real-time attendance data and family contact information.
target_learning_goals: Increasing family engagement and supporting student attendance
examples: The PowerSchool Attendance Intervention app auto-populates parent or student names and real-time attendance data into messaging templates used for two-way text and email communication with families.
